title: Can the number-grid payload seed a rune key?
question: Do the two canonical 256-byte grid payloads yield an English-scoring LP2 key under four named PRFs at offset zero?
reader_question: If we stretch the hidden 256-byte grid into a key, does it reveal the opening runes?
summary: The best of 32 fixed payload-derived keys stayed below the predeclared English and shuffled-text thresholds. Four planted controls passed the same decoder.
finding: No candidate in this 32-case corner passed: best score −7.105, shuffled-null ceiling −7.001, required score −5.5. Four planted controls each scored −4.17 with 98.9% character recovery.
limitations: Only the first 400 runes, two raw canonical payloads, four named PRFs, two byte reductions, two signs, forward direction, no Atbash and offset zero. This does not replay the full upstream B-05 search or rule out other payload uses or languages.
next_steps: If the grid suggests a specific alternate byte reading or key alignment, state it in advance and run the planted control and the same null comparison before expanding the search.

scope.representation: Key source: two 256-byte readings of the grid on LP2-49–51. Decode target: first 400 runes of the pinned stream, covering LP2-00 and the opening 138 runes of LP2-01; no other rune pages are decoded.
scope.procedure: Run source planted controls; decode the fixed 32 keys; compare source English score against its declared threshold and 200 shuffled-head controls.
scope.parameters: Two raw 256-byte payloads × four PRFs × two reductions × two signs; beam width 120, maximum three key skips, offset 0, forward, no Atbash.
scope.exclusions: No full-page decode or replay of the full B-05 sweep; no transformed payloads, further PRFs, reversed/Atbash keys, nonzero offsets, contested-byte variants or non-English scores.

review.reviewer: Pinned-source replay with independent result and PRF checks

reproduction.environment: Python 3 with cryptography; pinned upstream source and its MIT license bundled. A full deterministic replay runs four planted controls, 200 shuffled heads and 32 candidates.

visuals.caption: The fixed manuscript candidates stayed below the shuffled-text ceiling and the required English-score threshold; planted controls passed.

family.title: Keys derived from the number-grid payload
family.question: Does a fixed expansion of the grid payload yield a readable rune stream?

variant.label: Two raw payloads and four generators

article:
## Finding

We tested whether the 256-byte number-grid payload could supply a **rune-by-rune key** for Liber Primus. In this fixed 32-case screen, **none passed** the source's English-score threshold. The best candidate scored **−7.105**, below both the required **−5.5** and the highest of 200 shuffled-text controls (**−7.001**). A higher score is better.

![Scores for planted controls, the best manuscript candidate, the shuffled-text ceiling and the required threshold.](experiments/records/grid-payload-prf-seed-corner/score-comparison.svg)

The decoder was capable of recognizing a supplied key. Four planted controls, one per generator, recovered **98.9%** of characters and scored **−4.17**. This makes the negative result meaningful for the fixed cases below; it does not prove the payload has no role elsewhere.

## What was tested

The [pinned B-05 source](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus/analysis/round13/B05/PREREG.md) supplies two 256-byte readings of the number grid. Each was used directly as a seed for SHA-256 counter mode, RC4, HMAC-DRBG-SHA256 or AES-256-CTR. For each generator we tried both byte-to-rune reductions and both addition signs: **2 × 4 × 2 × 2 = 32** keys. The source's skip-aware beam decoded the first 400 unsolved runes with a forward key starting at offset zero.

This is a deliberately small corner of B-05, whose published search also included transformed payloads, more generators, reverse keys, Atbash, offsets, and contested-byte variations. We did not revalidate that whole published sweep here. Nor does an English-scoring failure exclude non-English plaintext or a different way to use the grid.

## Reproduce

The [saved result](experiments/records/grid-payload-prf-seed-corner/results.json) lists all 32 scores. From the repository root, install Python 3 and `cryptography`, then run:

```text
python experiments/records/grid-payload-prf-seed-corner/run.py --check
python experiments/records/grid-payload-prf-seed-corner/check.py
```

The first command reruns the four planted controls, 200 shuffles and 32 candidates using bundled pinned source in a temporary folder. The second checks the case grid, threshold, payload hashes and independent PRF spot checks. The [source manifest](experiments/records/grid-payload-prf-seed-corner/source-manifest.json) pins each upstream file by Git blob and SHA-256; the source is bundled under its MIT license.
